units: <cite ref="Chullin 142a:9">Ḥull. 142ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="L00354"><he>לָחַךְ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Pesachim 113b:2">Pes. 113ᵇ</cite> <he>המדבר אחד בפה ואחד בלב</he> he who speaks one way with his mouth, and another way in his heart.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1:31">Ex. R. s. 1</cite> (play on <he>בפרך</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 1:13">Ex. I, 13</cite>) <he>בפה רך</he> with soft (persuasive) speech; <cite ref="Sotah 11b">Sot. 11ᵇ</cite>. Tanḥ. Kor. 9 <he>עד שהביאתו לפִי הארץ וכ׳</he> until it (the fire) brought him to the opening of the earth, among those that were swallowed up; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 752:4">Yalk. Num. 752</cite>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 140b:8">Sabb. 140ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>בהמה שפִּיהָ יפה</he> a beast whose mouth is clean (that does not drop saliva when eating; oth. opin.: that is fastidious about its food), opp. <he>שפיה רעה</he>; a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 1:6">Keth. I, 6</cite>, a. e. <he>לא מִפּיהָ וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="H00671"><he>חָיָה</he></cite>.
Shebu. IV, 1 מִפִּי עצמו (an oath) out of his own mouth (‘I swear that I know no testimony in thy case’), מפי אחרים administered by others.—בְּעַל פה or על פה by word of mouth.
<cite ref="Gittin 72b:4">Gitt. 72ᵇ</cite> top <he>אי אמר ר׳ יוסי בעל פה</he> whether R. Yose had the same opinion in the case of a verbal condition.
<cite ref="Gittin 60b:6">Ib. 60ᵇ</cite> <he>תורה רוב בכתב ומיעוט על פה</he> of the interpretations of the Law, the larger portion rests on the written text, the smaller on oral tradition.

Ib. דברים שבכתב … על פה דברים שבעל פה וכ׳ written things (Biblical passages) must not be recited from memory, verbally transmitted words must not be recited from writing.—תורה שבעל פה (abbrev. שבע״פ) oral law.
<cite ref="Yoma 28b:10">Yoma 28ᵇ</cite>, a. fr., v. <cite ref="K01341"><he>כְּתָב</he></cite>.—לְפִי

<cite ref="Bava Batra 11b:6">B. Bath. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>לפי בני אדם</he> in proportion to the number of inhabitants of a house; <he>לפי פתחים</he> in proportion to the number of entrances (of a building); a. fr.—
senses.label: a

units: Snh. VII, 4 לפי שבאת לפיכך וכ׳ … because a human being has gone to ruin through it, therefore &c.; a. fr., v. לְפִיכָךְ.—Trnsf. any orifice.

<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 5:6">Ab. V, 6</cite> <he>פי הארץ</he> the opening of the earth (that swallowed Korah); <he>פי הבאר</he> the opening for the well (<cite ref="Numbers 21:16">Num. XXI, 16</cite>).—
Nidd. 16ᵇ רוק בתוך הפה spittle in the mouth, euphem. for blood in the orifice of the matrix.

Snh. 100ᵃ (play on ת̇ר̇ופ̇ה̇, Ez. XLVII, 12) להת̇יר̇ פ̇ה̇ של מטה to open the lower orifice (the womb of the childless), opp. פה של מעלה the mouth; ib. להתיר פה עקרות; Men. 98ᵃ; a. fr.—Pl. a) פִּיּוֹת.

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2:29">Deut. R. s. 2</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Zechariah 13:8">Zech. XIII, 8</cite>) <he>הפ׳ שאומרים שתי וכ׳</he> those mouths that say, there are two powers (good and evil).

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:4:4">Cant. R. to IV, 4</cite> (play on <he>תלפיות</he>, <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:4:4">ib.</cite>) <he>ספר שאמרוהו פ׳ הרבה</he> the book (<cite ref="V00451"><he>תִּלִּים</he></cite>, Psalms) which many mouths have indited (the book of many authors).
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:4:4">Ib.</cite> <he>ת̇ל̇ שמתפללין בו כל פ׳</he> the mound (Temple ruins) towards which all mouths are directed in prayer; <cite ref="Berakhot 30a">Ber. 30ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 5a:4">Ib. 5ᵃ</cite> (expl. <cite ref="Q00786"><he>פיפיות</he></cite>, <cite ref="Psalms 149:6">Ps. CXLIX, 6</cite>) <he>חרב של שתי פ׳</he> a two-edged sword; a. fr.—
Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXVIII שתי פ׳ two faces, v. פִּינָּה.—b) פִּיפִיּוֹת.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 18:22">Num. R. s. 18</cite> <he>באותה … פ׳ הרבה</he> at that moment many mouths of the earth were opened (<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 752:4">Yalk. ib. 752</cite> <cite ref="Q00605"><he>פיות</he></cite>).—
senses.label: b
